source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with diabetes asks why the nurse wants family members at an insulin class. What is the BEST reply?
options: 'Your family is at risk for diabetes too.'
'They'll give your insulin from now on.'
'They can support you in adjusting your care.'
questions.rationale: Families are included in diabetes education to help with adjustments to the regimen. Supportive family involvement helps the client become independent in care.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q813 (PDF p. 1047)
questions.quote: Families and significant others may be included in diabetes education to assist with adjustments of the diabetic regimen.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with ruptured esophageal varices and a history of alcohol abuse says, 'I deserve this.' Which response is MOST therapeutic?
options: 'Would you like to see the chaplain?'
'Is there some reason you feel you deserve this?'
questions.rationale: An open-ended response invites the client to talk and helps the nurse get an accurate history of alcohol intake, which a shamed client might hide.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q847 (PDF p. 1084)
questions.quote: It is important to obtain an accurate history regarding the client’s alcohol intake.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with jaundice has pruritus. Which statement needs MORE teaching?
options: 'A tepid bath will ease the itch.'
'I'll keep the house warm and cozy.'
questions.rationale: Bile salts deposited in the skin cause the itching. A cool environment minimizes it; warmth worsens it.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1065 (PDF p. 1347)
questions.quote: The client would be instructed to keep the house temperature cool in order to minimize the itching.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with Addison's disease is monitored for hyperkalemia. Which finding is MOST concerning?
questions.rationale: Low aldosterone in Addison's disease causes potassium retention. The most harmful effect of hyperkalemia is on cardiac function.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1113 (PDF p. 1397)
questions.quote: The most harmful consequence of hyperkalemia is its effect on cardiac function.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which intervention is ESSENTIAL in the care plan after a bilateral adrenalectomy?
questions.rationale: Adrenalectomy can lead to adrenal insufficiency, and adrenal hormones are needed to respond to stress. Stress can trigger adrenal crisis.
explanations: Correct: stress can trigger adrenal crisis.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1147 (PDF p. 1434)
questions.quote: Adrenal hormones are essential to maintaining homeostasis in response to stressors.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which outcome shows that nutrition care for a client with Graves' disease is successful?
options: She eats less to control appetite
She limits calories to 1,200 a day
questions.rationale: Graves' disease causes a hypercatabolic state with weight loss despite increased appetite. The goal is no further weight loss and a gradual return to ideal weight.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1239 (PDF p. 1532)
questions.quote: it is a nutritional goal that the client will not lose additional weight

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which findings of thyroid storm require IMMEDIATE intervention?
questions.rationale: Excess thyroid hormone sharply raises the metabolic rate, causing fever, tachycardia, and hypertension. Quick action is needed because death can follow.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1257 (PDF p. 1558)
questions.quote: causing the manifestations of thyroid storm such as fever, tachycardia, and hypertension.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which fear is a REALISTIC source of anxiety before thyroidectomy?
questions.rationale: The incision is in the neck, so fear of a large scar is realistic. There are no specific dietary restrictions after discharge.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1261 (PDF p. 1562)
questions.quote: Because the incision is in the neck area, the client may be fearful of having a large scar postoperatively.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which finding suggests perforation in a client with peptic ulcer disease?
questions.rationale: Sudden, severe abdominal pain signals perforation. The pulse becomes weak and rapid, and bowel sounds may be absent. A positive guaiac shows bleeding, not necessarily perforation.
explanations: The pulse becomes weak and rapid.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1294 (PDF p. 1595)
questions.quote: Sudden, severe abdominal pain is a sign of perforation.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which MODIFIABLE risk factor for colorectal cancer should the nurse emphasize?
questions.rationale: A high-fat, low-fiber diet can be changed. Age, family history, and ulcerative colitis cannot.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1395 (PDF p. 1699)
questions.quote: Modifiable risk factors are those that can be reduced and include a high-fat and low-fiber diet.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should a client with GERD sleep to reduce reflux?
options: Head of bed raised about 30 degrees
questions.rationale: The client stays upright 1 to 2 hours after meals and sleeps with the head of the bed raised about 30 degrees (on 8- to 12-inch blocks). Lying flat increases reflux.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1396 (PDF p. 1700)
questions.quote: sleep with the head of the bed elevated to approximately 30 degrees

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should the client be positioned for abdominal paracentesis?
questions.rationale: Semi-Fowler's or upright on the edge of the bed with feet supported lets the intestines float back and helps prevent laceration.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1404 (PDF p. 1710)
questions.quote: This position allows the intestine to float posteriorly and helps prevent laceration during catheter insertion.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with chronic ulcerative colitis has anemia. What is the MOST likely cause?
questions.rationale: Ulcerative colitis causes repeated small blood losses during exacerbations, with bloody stools, leading to anemia.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1464 (PDF p. 1773)
questions.quote: The client with chronic ulcerative colitis is most likely anemic as a result of chronic blood loss in small amounts

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which statement shows a client with diabetes understands the signs of HYPERglycemia?
options: 'I'll feel tired, have dry skin, and urinate more.'
'I'll take an extra pill if sugar is high.'
questions.rationale: Fatigue, dry skin, polyuria, and polydipsia are classic hyperglycemia signs. Sweating, shakiness, and hunger suggest hypoglycemia.
explanations: Doses are not changed by the client.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1470 (PDF p. 1779)
questions.quote: Fatigue, dry skin, polyuria, and polydipsia are classic symptoms of hyperglycemia.
